title: Participation in projects

blocks.heading: Participation in projects
blocks.text: Rural and urban projects can connect women’s organisations, self-help groups and agencies to skills, finance or service needs. Assess retained benefits, meaningful decisions and the inclusion of less-represented participants. A project called a women’s scheme does not establish impact.
context_tags: original teaching; fictional examples where stated

blocks.heading: A practical access test
blocks.text: Explain which fictional project better meets an inclusive skills aim: A trains many urban participants but excludes remote applicants through travel costs; B trains fewer initially and funds a workable rural access route. B better addresses the stated inclusion gap, while A has greater immediate volume. Choice depends on the weight given to reaching excluded applicants and maintaining quality; training totals alone do not establish inclusive benefit.
context_tags: original teaching; fictional examples where stated

blocks.heading: Connect the ideas
blocks.text: Connect to traditional roles (6.1), education (7.3) and research (10.1). Use evidence about resources, voice and practical access. Fictional cases do not establish current law, service availability or a diagnosis about any individual.
